Board request (DM msg 297, 2026-08-31): roles next to names in the DM list section of the chat app.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE (SMALL) TASK: the data already flows end-to-end. lib/personnel.js returns title/class/team per dossier, and GET /api/roster (server.js ~line 135) already ships 'title' in every roster row. Today the web client only exposes it as a hover tooltip: public/app.js rosterRow() sets name.title = emp.title (HTML title attribute, line ~259). So this is a pure frontend change — render the title as visible text (e.g. a muted secondary line or inline suffix in .roster-row), touching public/app.js + public/style.css only. No server, parser, or schema changes. Keep the AS-18 pin/sort behavior and the AS-23 responsive layout intact (long titles like 'Cofounder & Chief Technology Officer' must truncate gracefully on narrow widths). Consider also showing the title in the non-roster DM rows' tooltip-equivalent if trivial, but the roster list is the ask.

Deliberately split from the org-chart-visualizer task (created same tick): this is self-contained UI polish shippable in one small diff; the visualizer is a new surface with an API addition and a validator. Coupling them would hold a one-hour change hostage to a multi-day one.

Acceptance: active-roster sidebar rows show each employee's title visibly (not tooltip-only); layout holds on mobile widths; existing dm-sort/pin tests still pass.

Internal tooling — proceeds without per-task board green-light per board directive DM msg 230; default implementer agent:developer-marcus.
data.title: Chat sidebar: show role/title next to names in the DM roster list

data.body: CTO ordering call (board DM msg 323). Rank 6. Small, board-requested, pure frontend (the roster row already carries title; it is buried in a hover tooltip). Behind the product line and AS-34 by policy, not by size.
Board directive (DM msg 394): all chat issues ship. Cluster order 5/6 — roster roles/titles; cosmetic, after the functional items.

Pulled as cluster item 4/6. Board request from the same DM as the org chart (msg 297), deliberately split from it as self-contained UI polish, and now genuinely small because AS-33 landed the surface it sits beside.

Two things changed since this description was written that the planner should read rather than inherit. First, AS-33 added an org-chart view rendering name, title, class and team from the same roster rows — so the sidebar's title suffix and the chart's node label are now two renderings of one field, and the plan should say whether they share a formatter or diverge deliberately. Second, AS-33 extended the structure-first lexical guard to a second module; a third rendering path arriving in the same file set means the same question applies again.

The description says the data already flows end to end and this is a pure frontend change. Verify that rather than assuming it: AS-33 touched the roster mapping to add the reporting edge, so the row shape moved after this description was written.

Marcus keeps it — already the assignee, and he wrote both the roster sidebar and the org chart that now sit next to each other.

Note for the planner: this is the smallest remaining task in the cluster and the plan should be sized accordingly. The discipline that matters here is not length — it is the responsive claim. Titles in this company run to 'Cofounder & Chief Technology Officer', the sidebar is narrow, and the last screen task's only near-miss was a viewport measurement that lied. Whatever the plan says about truncation at narrow widths must be checkable, and the instrument must measure the viewport it actually got.

Plan written. Decisions: (1) two formatters, not one — the sidebar renders title alone, the org chart keeps its title·class·team meta line; the shared layer is the field in lib/personnel.js, not the presentation, and AC7 pins the divergence so it fails as drift rather than surprising someone. (2) Truncation is a dedicated .roster-title block with nowrap+overflow:hidden+ellipsis — load-bearing, since #roster-list li.roster-row sets white-space: normal and a long title would otherwise wrap and grow the row. The lexical test proves the rule was written; the one-line contract is geometry and is measured in a browser (all title heights equal, at least one row clipped so the check is not vacuous). (3) Tooltip stays, and is added to the clipped element too. (4) The responsive instrument aborts unless it measures the sidebar width it was asked for, and prints cardinality before quantification — screenshots are illustration, the console readings are the evidence. (5) Class and team stay out of the sidebar. 10 ACs, 4 falsification recipes, three-file scope, baseline 233 pass / 0 fail.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-32 on feat/AS-32-roster-titles, per the plan: a dedicated title element with its own ellipsis rule (load-bearing, since roster rows set white-space: normal and the inherited rule never reaches them), two formatters not one with a test pinning the divergence, tooltip kept and added to the clipped element, and the geometry asserted rather than only the CSS text.

Implementation complete (AS-32). Commit 5be7041 on feat/AS-32-roster-titles. Worktree clean, nothing pushed, nothing merged. FILES + DIFF SIZE — exactly the three files in plan §2 (AC10): apps/chat/public/app.js | 11 +++++- apps/chat/public/style.css | 10 +++++ apps/chat/test/api.test.js | 99 ++++++++++++++++ 3 files changed, 119 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-) Stop-and-explain line (300) NOT approached: 119 lines, 40% of budget. Plan §7 estimate (~10 app / ~7 CSS / ~60 test) was accurate on app.js and CSS; the test came in at 99 rather than ~60 because R3(a)'s hostile-root leg lives inside the AC7 case. R4 SCOPE ASSERTION: `git diff --stat master...HEAD --` over dm-sort.js, test/dm-sort.test.js, server.js, lib/personnel.js, public/org-chart.js, public/index.html prints NOTHING. dm-sort.js and test/dm-sort.test.js byte-identical (AC6). §3.6 held. SUITE — before: 233 pass / 0 fail. After: 235 pass / 0 fail (5.37s). Matches plan §6.0 exactly. LITERALS THAT MOVED (grep -oF … | wc -l, never grep -c). 10 of 11 match the plan's predicted after-values; one is off and flagged as deviation D1: roster-title app.js 0 -> 1 as predicted emp.title app.js 1 -> 4 PREDICTED 3 — see D1 .innerHTML app.js 0 -> 0 as predicted insertAdjacentHTML app.js 0 -> 0 as predicted outerHTML app.js 0 -> 0 as predicted document.write app.js 0 -> 0 as predicted emp.class app.js 0 -> 0 as predicted (not-moving set held) emp.team app.js 0 -> 0 as predicted (not-moving set held) .roster-title style.css 0 -> 2 as predicted text-overflow style.css 1 -> 2 as predicted 'api: AS-32' api.test 0 -> 2 (>=2 satisfied; 3 counting the section header) FALSIFICATION RECIPES — all against fresh scratch copies outside the worktree (cp -R apps/chat "$SCRATCH/chat-rN"). No in-place mutation anywhere, so no restore was needed; proven below regardless. Each harness asserted the mutation applied BEFORE running tests and aborts on a count mismatch. R1 — the title line is actually rendered. Step 0: `grep -oF 'api: AS-32' test/api.test.js | wc -l` == 2. Assert-applied, scoped to the region the mutation edits: `awk '/^function rosterRow\(emp\) \{/,/^\}/' public/app.js | grep -oF 'roster-title' | wc -l` 1 -> 0. Observed failing set: EXACTLY ONE — 'api: AS-32 — served app.js renders the roster title through el() and shows title alone' Predicted one, observed one, same case. (34 tests / 33 pass / 1 fail.) R2 — the truncation rule is real. Assert-applied both ways as the plan requires: whole-file `text-overflow` 2 -> 1 AND `sed -n '/^\.roster-title {/,/^}/p' | grep -oF 'text-overflow' | wc -l` 1 -> 0. Observed failing set: EXACTLY ONE — 'api: AS-32 — style.css truncates the roster title to one line' Predicted one, observed one, same case. Note the value of the region scoping is now measured, not asserted: with the declaration gone the whole-file count is still 1, so an unscoped `includes('text-overflow')` assertion would have passed against the broken file. R3(a) — the endpoint ships the field verbatim. Scratch root (mkdtemp + cpSync of test/fixtures/repo, plus personnel/hostile.md; the shared fixture is never mutated — other tests assert its roster membership). GET /api/roster returns title === '' unchanged, 30 bytes on the wire. The server does not escape; a test expecting it to would assert a defence that does not exist. Lives inside the AC7 case and passes. R3(b) — falsify the client-side defence. Replaced the el() line + role.title with `el('div','roster-title'); role.innerHTML = emp.title;`. Assert-applied: whole-file `.innerHTML` 0 -> 1 AND scoped to rosterRow 0 -> 1. Ran the FULL suite for a complete cardinality, not just api.test.js. PREDICTED: exactly 3 cases. OBSERVED: exactly 4 (235 tests / 231 pass / 4 fail): 'api: AS-26 — msg-refs.js and markdown.js are served; index.html ships the file modal' (predicted) 'api: AS-54 — served app.js autolinks through markdown.js and never inside a markdown link' (predicted) 'api: AS-32 — served app.js renders the roster title through el() and shows title alone' (predicted) 'api: AS-33 — org-chart.js is served, imported, and holds the no-innerHTML line' (NOT predicted) This is deviation D2 — a wider set than predicted, which the plan itself says is a finding. Cause below; no code change follows from it. R3(c) — browser leg, UNMUTATED build, scratch root (personnel/ never written to). Hostile dossier's title rendered as the literal characters: IMGS in #roster-list = 0, IMGS in the whole document = 0, .roster-title.children.length = 0, textContent === '' at 30 bytes — byte-identical to the wire value. el()/textContent is the only defence between a dossier field and the DOM, and it holds. GEOMETRY (§3.5 / AC3, AC4, AC5, AC9). Instrument driven over CDP against the cached chrome-headless-shell — zero new dependencies (node 24's built-in WebSocket), ephemeral ports, everything torn down. asc-chat-server-1 (8347) and asc-invoicing-web-1 (8348) untouched and still up. The instrument measures the viewport it actually got and throws if it differs from TARGET; the abort was never taken, so every width below is measured, not asserted by a flag. Pass A, real personnel titles (10 active employees): DESKTOP VIEWPORT {"innerWidth":1280,"client":1280,"sidebar":240} CARDINALITY {"rows":10,"titles":10} (10 active dossiers, all with non-empty title) CHILDREN ["roster-top","roster-title","roster-status"] HEIGHTS [16] OVERFLOW {"sbScroll":240,"sbClient":240,"doc":1280} CLIPPED [] IMGS 0 MOBILE VIEWPORT {"innerWidth":375,"client":375,"sidebar":280} CARDINALITY {"rows":10,"titles":10} CHILDREN ["roster-top","roster-title","roster-status"] HEIGHTS [16] OVERFLOW {"sbScroll":280,"sbClient":280,"doc":375} CLIPPED [] IMGS 0 TOOLTIP ["Cofounder & Chief Executive Officer","Cofounder & Chief Executive Officer"] at both widths — full string from both hover targets (AC5). CLIPPED was EMPTY at both widths. Per the plan that makes the truncation reading vacuous, so I did not record it as a pass — I re-ran against a temporarily lengthened title, in the scratch root, exactly as §3.5 directs. Owen's real title ("Cofounder & Chief Technology Officer") does in fact fit in the 240px column at 11px; the plan's parenthetical that it clips there is wrong (deviation D3). Pass B, scratch root + one lengthened title (83 chars), rule PRESENT: DESKTOP VIEWPORT {"innerWidth":1280,"client":1280,"sidebar":240} CARDINALITY {"rows":11,"titles":11} HEIGHTS [16] ROW_HEIGHTS [60] OVERFLOW {"sbScroll":240,"sbClient":240,"doc":1280} CLIPPED ["Cofounder & Chief Technology Officer, Platform Reliability and Developer Experience"] MOBILE VIEWPORT {"innerWidth":375,"client":375,"sidebar":280} CARDINALITY {"rows":11,"titles":11} HEIGHTS [16] ROW_HEIGHTS [84] OVERFLOW {"sbScroll":280,"sbClient":280,"doc":375} CLIPPED ["Cofounder & Chief Technology Officer, Platform Reliability and Developer Experience"] AC3 (one distinct height), AC4 (no horizontal overflow) and the ellipsis actually engaging are all satisfied non-vacuously. Row height is a single value across all 11 rows at each width — the "one fixed height whatever the title's length" contract, measured. Pass C, instrument sanity — a geometric check only ever seen reporting HEIGHTS==[16] has proven nothing, so I broke it. Single-variable control: deleted ONLY `white-space: nowrap` from inside the .roster-title body, leaving font-size and the ellipsis declaration in place. Assert-applied scoped: .roster-title nowrap 1 -> 0, .roster-title ellipsis still 1, whole-file nowrap 1 (the older #sidebar li rule). Same lengthened title, same 240px measured width: HEIGHTS [16,48] ROW_HEIGHTS [60,92] CLIPPED [] Two distinct title heights (48 == three 16px lines) and a row 32px taller. So the instrument does see a wrap, the reading in Pass B is not vacuous, and the plan's §3.2 claim that the rule is load-bearing rather than decorative is now measured rather than argued. (A first control that deleted the whole rule block gave HEIGHTS [41,20,61]; I discarded it as evidence because removing font-size confounds the height delta, and re-ran the isolated mutation above.) Screenshots (illustration only; the readings above are the evidence) at $SCRATCH/agent-developer-marcus/as32-{desktop,mobile,desktop-long,mobile-long,desktop-nocss}.png. RESTORATION / HYGIENE: no in-place mutation was performed, so nothing needed restoring. Proven anyway — content-hash manifest of the three files, disk vs committed blob: app.js 8037d4e67d364fd2 MATCH, style.css 96c2618cdf3ef052 MATCH, api.test.js 5fe38da99b44b364 MATCH; `git diff --exit-code` clean; `git status --porcelain` empty in the AS-32 worktree AND in the main checkout. personnel/ never written to (all hostile and lengthened dossiers went to scratch roots). .worktrees/AS-45 untouched. No stray listeners, no surviving chrome-headless-shell. DEVIATIONS D1. `emp.title` in app.js landed at 4 occurrences, not the plan's predicted 3. No code deviation: the block I committed is byte-identical to the §4 snippet, which itself contains three (`if (emp.title)`, the el() argument, `role.title = emp.title`) on top of the pre-existing `name.title = emp.title`. The §6.0 table undercounted its own snippet by one, apparently not counting the guard. Baseline 1 and every other predicted value were exact. D2. R3(b)'s failing set is 4, not 3. The plan's reasoning for treating an AS-33 failure as a finding is factually wrong: 'api: AS-33 — org-chart.js is served…' does not only guard org-chart.js — api.test.js:1014 is `assert.doesNotMatch(app, /\.innerHTML/)` against the served app.js, deliberately, with a comment saying so. There are exactly THREE whole-file app.js innerHTML guards in the suite (api.test.js:702 AS-26, :906 AS-54, :1014 AS-33); §6 R3(b) enumerated two of three. The wider set is a correct guard firing correctly, not a defect — but it means the plan's predicted set was wrong, and I am recording it rather than quietly accepting a mismatch. Nothing in the implementation changes. D3. §3.5's "CLIPPED non-empty at the 240px desktop width (Owen's title clips there)" does not hold against the real roster: no real title clips at 240px, so the natural reading is vacuous. Handled by the escape hatch the same clause provides — said so, and re-ran against a lengthened title — rather than recording an empty CLIPPED as a pass. Worth noting for whoever maintains this: with today's titles, AC3/AC4 are satisfied trivially, and the truncation contract only has teeth once someone's title exceeds ~208px of content width. No open questions were reopened: Q1 (own line under the name), Q2 (11px/#bfa8c0, matching .roster-status) and Q3 (sink list kept local to the AS-32 case, existing tests untouched) all ship at their plan defaults. WHAT THE REVIEWER SHOULD LOOK AT FIRST: D2 — whether my reading of api.test.js:1014 is right and the plan's R3(b) prediction was simply wrong, since that is the one place my observations contradict the plan on a matter of fact rather than arithmetic. Then Pass C, which is the only evidence that the geometric truncation check can fail at all; if that control is unconvincing, AC3 is not really proven. Then the AC7 complete-class-set deepEqual (api.test.js), which is the AS-54 lesson applied — confirm it would fail on a stray extra class, not merely a missing one.

Orchestrator verification and review assignment.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: exactly the three declared files, personnel/ untouched, 119 insertions against a 300-line stop-and-explain line — 40 percent of budget, so the estimate held.

D2 CONFIRMED, and the implementer is right against the plan. I grepped it myself: api.test.js carries THREE whole-file innerHTML guards on the served app.js, at lines 702, 906 and 1014, each with the identical message. The plan's section 6 enumerated two. So four failing cases was the correct observation and the prediction was wrong — a correct guard firing correctly. He recorded the mismatch rather than quietly accepting it, which is the behaviour the discipline is for.

Worth noting for whoever picks up AS-72, which already owns a finding in this file: there are now three byte-identical copies of the same assertion in one test file, added by three different tasks that each extended the guard without noticing the previous extension. That is not a defect and none of them is wrong — but a fourth screen task will add a fourth, and the count is the thing that keeps surprising predictions.

D3 IS THE FINDING THAT MATTERS, and it is a negative result reported honestly. The plan asserted a specific real title clips at the sidebar width. It does not — nothing in the current roster clips at either width, and the plan itself defines an empty clipped set as vacuous. Rather than record an empty result as a pass, he took the clause's own escape hatch, said so, and re-ran against a lengthened title in a scratch root to prove the mechanism engages. The standing consequence he states plainly: with today's titles the truncation contract has no teeth until someone's title exceeds roughly 208px of content width. That is exactly the kind of guarantee that would otherwise sit green and untested until the day it mattered.

He also discarded his own first control as confounded — deleting the whole rule block changed font-size too, so the height delta had two causes — and re-ran an isolated mutation. He then flagged that control as the single piece of evidence the geometric check can fail at all, and told the reviewer to attack it first. An implementer naming the weakest link in his own evidence is worth more than the evidence.

FOR THE BOARD, NOT FOR THIS REVIEW: the plan's open question 1 records that the own-line versus inline choice is reversible in one CSS rule if the board disagrees on sight. Forrest asked for this feature; how it looks is his call and the screenshot is the artifact for it. I will put it in front of him at merge rather than mid-review.

REVIEW: assigning agent:qa-ruben. Marcus implemented, so implementer != reviewer holds; Priya took AS-33 last tick. Ruben's brief should start where the implementer pointed — the isolated control is the only evidence the geometric assertion can fail, and if it does not convince, the truncation criterion is not really proven.

QA review (agent:qa-ruben) — AS-32. VERDICT: PASS. 10 of 10 acceptance criteria met. No defect found. Six findings recorded, all non-blocking; four are gaps in the plan's guard set, not in the implementation. No inline fixes were needed and none were made — the branch is exactly as the implementer left it (commit 5be7041). READ ORDER (disclosed): CLAUDE.md Review Gate + Review Rework Loop, then the plan, then the task description alone (piped out of `lattice show --json`), then the diff cold, then the tests as documents. I ran every recipe and wrote all verdicts down BEFORE opening the comment stream. I read the implementer's report and the orchestrator's verification LAST. I did not take a walkthrough. --- CARDINALITY BEFORE QUANTIFICATION --- Examined: 3 changed files, 119 insertions / 1 deletion, 1 commit. Suite: 235 cases on the branch (233 on master), run 9 times end to end. 34 cases in api.test.js, run 8 times. 8 mutation recipes executed (R1, R2, R3b, R5, R6, R7, R8, R9, R10 — R6 and R9 each aborted once on a wrong prediction of my own and were re-run). 5 browser geometry passes at 2 widths each = 10 measured viewports. 4 scratch repo roots (real / lengthened / hostile / empty-title). 11 personnel dossiers censused, 10 active, 10 with a non-empty title. Of those: 10/10 ACs pass, 235/235 tests pass, 10/10 viewports measured with the abort never taken, 4/4 scratch roots behaved as specified. --- WHAT I RAN --- Full suite on master (233 pass / 0 fail) and on the branch (235 pass / 0 fail, 5.36s). All mutations on scratch copies OUTSIDE the worktree (`cp -R` into my scratchpad); the worktree was never mutated. Every harness asserts the mutation applied SCOPED to the region it edits and hard-aborts before running anything if the count is not the predicted one — `grep -c` never used; occurrence counts via split/length or `grep -oF | wc -l`. --- PER-AC VERDICT (10/10) --- AC1 PASS. CHILDREN is ["roster-top","roster-title","roster-status"] on all 10 rows at 240px and all 10 at 280px. Measured, not inferred: the lexical test cannot see DOM order. AC2 PASS. Independently exercised on a 4th scratch root with an active dossier whose `title:` is empty — the reports do not cover this case. CARDINALITY {"rows":11,"titles":10}; that row's children are exactly ["roster-top","roster-status"]; zero .roster-title elements; no title="" on a title element. Emitted:
  • ...
    idle
    • . AC3 PASS. HEIGHTS [16] — one distinct value — at both widths on the real roster, AND with a 388px-wide title present. Proven non-vacuous by controls (below). AC4 PASS. 240px: sbScroll 240 / sbClient 240. 280px: sbScroll 280 / sbClient 280. Holds on all four roots including the 388px title and the hostile string. AC5 PASS. TOOLTIP {"title0":"Cofounder & Chief Executive Officer","name0":"Cofounder & Chief Executive Officer"} at both widths — full string from both hover targets. AC6 PASS. dm-sort.js, test/dm-sort.test.js, test/org-chart.test.js, test/personnel.test.js byte-identical master vs branch (sha256 compared). 233 -> 235, 0 fail. .pin-toggle count 10/10 rows, CSS untouched. AC7 PASS, and proven in BOTH directions. R1 (missing class) fails it; R5 (stray EXTRA class, the AS-54 lesson) fails it — I added `el('div', 'roster-extra', 'x')` to rosterRow and the deepEqual reported actual with 'roster-extra' inserted vs expected without it. Sinks: 0 occurrences each of .innerHTML / insertAdjacentHTML / outerHTML / document.write. emp.class 0, emp.team 0 in the region. AC8 PASS. R2 and R6 both fail it. The region scoping is load-bearing and I measured that rather than assuming it: with the declaration deleted the WHOLE-FILE `text-overflow` count is still 1 (the older #sidebar li rule at L50), so an unscoped assertion would have passed against the broken file. AC9 PASS via the escape hatch the clause itself defines. CLIPPED was EMPTY at both widths on the real roster; per §3.5 that is vacuous, so I re-ran against a lengthened title in a scratch root. Readings verbatim below. AC10 PASS. Exactly the three files in §2. `git diff --stat master...branch --` over dm-sort.js, test/dm-sort.test.js, server.js, lib/personnel.js, org-chart.js, index.html prints nothing. No .lattice/ on the branch. --- MY OWN GEOMETRY READINGS (my instrument, my viewports, not inherited) --- Instrument: playwright 1.62.1 + chromium, installed ONLY in my scratchpad (repo and apps/chat/package.json untouched; zero new dependencies in the diff). Server booted from the branch worktree on an ephemeral loopback port against scratch repo roots. I started no container and touched none: asc-chat-server-1 (8347) and asc-invoicing-web-1 (8348) were up before and after, untouched. Nothing under personnel/ was ever written — every hostile/lengthened/empty dossier lives in a scratch root. No surviving browser processes. The instrument measures the sidebar width it actually GOT and hard-aborts if it differs from TARGET. The abort was never taken in 10 passes, so every width below is measured. PASS A — real roster (10 active dossiers, all titled): DESKTOP VIEWPORT {"innerWidth":1280,"client":1280,"sidebar":240,"dpr":1} ABORT null CARDINALITY {"rows":10,"titles":10} HEIGHTS [16] ROWHEIGHTS [60] CLIPPED [] OVERFLOW {"sbScroll":240,"sbClient":240,"doc":1280,"docClient":1280} IMGS 0 MOBILE VIEWPORT {"innerWidth":375,"client":375,"sidebar":280,"dpr":1} ABORT null CARDINALITY {"rows":10,"titles":10} HEIGHTS [16] ROWHEIGHTS [84] CLIPPED [] OVERFLOW {"sbScroll":280,"sbClient":280,"doc":375,"docClient":375} IMGS 0 (Note on the mobile leg: the drawer is ALREADY open on load at 375px — #app carries drawer-open and #sidebar computed transform is none. A scripted click on #sidebar-toggle therefore times out, intercepted by #brand. Pre-existing app behaviour, not this diff; recorded so the next reviewer does not chase it.) PASS B — same build, one lengthened title (75 chars) in a scratch root, rule PRESENT: DESKTOP sidebar 240 HEIGHTS [16] ROWHEIGHTS [60] OVERFLOW 240/240 CLIPPED ["Interim Deputy Assistant Vice President of Platform Reliability Engineering"] MOBILE sidebar 280 HEIGHTS [16] ROWHEIGHTS [84] OVERFLOW 280/280 CLIPPED ["Interim Deputy Assistant Vice President of Platform Reliability Engineering"] So the ellipsis engages at BOTH widths, height stays one line, no overflow. AC3/AC4 non-vacuous. I ALSO MEASURED THE HEADROOM, which neither report quantifies. Natural (unconstrained) text width vs available box, at 240px sidebar / 208px content box: Cofounder & Chief Technology Officer 200px natural vs 208px box -> 8px of headroom Cofounder & Chief Executive Officer 190px / 208px Software Engineer (full-stack) 157px / 208px Market Research Analyst 130px / 208px Brand & Visual Designer 127px / 208px UX Designer 66px, QA Engineer 65px / 208px At 280px (248px box) the widest real title has 48px of headroom. So the desktop margin is EIGHT PIXELS — roughly one and a half characters. The next C-level title one character longer clips in production. That is the sharp version of D3. --- JUDGMENT ON THE CONTROL (the thing I was asked to attack) --- ACCEPTED, and independently reproduced rather than taken on his numbers. I re-ran his isolated control myself: deleted ONLY `white-space: nowrap` from inside the .roster-title body, asserting single-variable-ness before measuring — scoped nowrap 1->0 while `text-overflow: ellipsis` stayed 1 and `font-size: 11px` stayed 1, so the height delta has exactly one cause. Whole-file nowrap stayed at 1 (the older #sidebar li rule), which again is why the scoping matters. Result on the lengthened title at a MEASURED 240px: HEIGHTS [16] -> [16,32], ROWHEIGHTS [60] -> [60,76]. At 280px: [16] -> [16,32], [84] -> [84,100]. My title wraps to 2 lines where his 83-char title gave 3 ([16,48]) — consistent, and the difference is title length, not instrument. So: the instrument demonstrably reports a wrap, the Pass B reading is not vacuous, and his decision to discard the first control as confounded (deleting the whole block moved font-size too, giving the height delta two causes) was correct methodology, not over-caution. The geometric assertion CAN fail, and I have seen it fail with my own instrument. AC3 is proven. --- THE QUESTION BEHIND IT: is a contract that sits green until someone's title gets long acceptable as shipped? --- I found a sharper version of the problem than either report states, and it changes the answer from "acceptable" to "acceptable, with a follow-up filed". FINDING 3 (below) — the truncation contract has NO standing automated guard at all. Not a weak one: none. I proved it. R8: leave the .roster-title rule body entirely intact and correct (all three declarations still assert-present, scoped), and add ONE later, more specific rule `#roster-list li.roster-row .roster-title { white-space: normal; }`. Full suite: 235 tests, 235 pass, 0 fail — completely green. Geometry on that same build with a lengthened title, at measured widths: HEIGHTS [16,32] at 240px and [16,32] at 280px, ROWHEIGHTS [60,76] and [84,100]. The rows grow, the contract in §3.2 is violated, and nothing in the suite notices. So the guard set proves the rule was WRITTEN (R2, R6 both fire correctly), but nothing proves it WORKS. Combined with 8px of real headroom, this is a guarantee that will sit green and untested until the day it matters — and on that day the test suite will still be green. My call, and I want to be explicit that I am not blocking on it: the implementer built precisely what the plan's AC8/AC9 specify — a lexical assertion plus a one-time manual measurement. He met the criteria. The gap is in the plan's AC set, and a 119-line UI-polish task is the wrong place to relitigate it mid-review. Sending a correct, working, well-evidenced change back to planning because its guard could be one notch stronger would spend review authority on the wrong fight.
